starter-motor-assembly.summary: A provisional M-terminal feed, insulated frame passage and four pigtails connect a two-feed/two-ground brush comparison around the commutator.
starter-motor-assembly.limits: Ford PMGR-family service text establishes the positive connector at M and frame grommet. J&N replacement photographs and Wagner cross-references support two feed brushes and two ground brushes, but not the installed identity, dimensions or clocking of this truck's brushes. Assigning model brushes1/4 to feed and2/3 to ground retains the existing assumed90degree layout. Winding packets and commutator segments remain aggregate subdivisions with no recovered interconnection diagram. No complete electrical circuit, current rating, brush-wear motion, torque or thermal prediction is claimed.

steps.title: Receive power at M
steps.text: The external eyelet and common conductor meet the solenoid motor terminal. Its route to the frame is a packaging study based on the sourced connector role, not a traced Ford wire path.

steps.title: Cross the frame through insulation
steps.text: A separate jacket and flanged grommet isolate the conductor from the bored frame. CAD checks establish clearances and solid separation, not dielectric strength or environmental sealing.

steps.title: Feed two brushes
steps.text: Two pigtails branch from the common feed and attach to brushes1and4. Their braid envelopes illustrate flexible electrical connections; strand count and movement as the brushes wear are not reconstructed.

steps.title: Return through the rear plate
steps.text: Pigtails from brushes2and3 reach a common metal bridge against the end plate and retaining screws. The comparison photo shows a common ground bracket, but this ring shape and screw-pad arrangement are assumed.

steps.title: Preserve the commutation boundary
steps.text: Stationary brushes meet the rotating commutator, but the displayed winding packets and24segments have no recovered electrical interconnection map. The feed and return geometry does not establish an operating motor circuit.

steps.title: Understand the magnetic structure
steps.text: The six permanent-magnet pole pieces establish the field architecture identified in the factory exploded view. Individual magnetic strength, armature current and electromagnetic torque are not simulated.

troubleshooting.title: Keep geometric checks within their scope
troubleshooting.text: Measured attachment patches and clearances do not determine brush resistance, spring load, current capacity or production fit. No live electrical test procedure is provided.

starter-solenoid-assembly.summary: Separate insulated coil-end routes connect aggregate pull/hold windings to S, M and frame through nonpenetrating attachment faces.
starter-solenoid-assembly.limits: Ford's conventional circuit and applicable continuity description support the winding endpoints. Lead paths, terminal clocking, sleeves and joining surfaces are provisional. Motor feed and four brush pigtails are represented in a separate comparison study; commutator-to-armature winding connections and vehicle cables remain absent. Geometric contact does not establish resistance, ampacity, loaded performance or production fit.

steps.title: Identify three terminals
steps.text: The small S terminal is distinct from the heavy B battery and M motor terminals. External battery and control cables remain open boundaries.

steps.title: Attach the pull winding
steps.text: Two provisional conductors join the pull-winding envelope to S and M at face interfaces. Individual winding turns, wire gauge and resistance remain unresolved.

steps.title: Attach the hold winding
steps.text: A separate S conductor reaches the hold-winding envelope; another conductor meets the shell's inner surface. The ground joint is a geometric study rather than a verified factory joining process.

steps.title: Keep the S routes separate
steps.text: The two S conductors meet separate patches of the same terminal. Their sleeves remain separated and terminate against the existing terminal insulator without occupying the same material.

steps.title: Close the power contacts
steps.text: The insulated moving bridge joins B to M at the prescribed closure pose. This shunts the pull winding in the declared conventional circuit while the hold winding remains supplied through S. Arcing, pressure and current are not simulated.

steps.title: Return the mechanism
steps.text: The spring and constrained linkage restore the prescribed resting geometry. Actual spring preload, electromagnetic release, loaded disengagement and production construction remain unresolved.

steps.title: Follow the modeled motor feed
steps.text: M also meets a provisional insulated conductor feeding two brush pigtails. Two other pigtails return through the rear plate. The assumed brush clocking and unresolved armature winding map do not establish a complete operating circuit.

troubleshooting.title: Distinguish geometry from current flow
troubleshooting.text: Zero-distance attachment faces and sampled insulation clearances cannot establish electrical resistance, current capacity or production reliability. The model does not provide a live high-current testing procedure.

starter-assembly.summary: A manual-transmission permanent-magnet gear-reduction starter converts battery energy into a brief, reduced-speed drive at the flywheel.
starter-assembly.limits: The displayed starter is stationary and disengaged. Its 132 modeled components are an architectural construction study, not a verified F2TZ11002ARM replica. Coil-end attachments, M feed and four brush pigtails are represented with provisional routing and brush clocking. Bellhousing/index-plate support, production mounting datums, overrunning internals, commutator winding connections, vehicle cables and loaded actuation remain unresolved.

steps.title: Make motor torque
steps.text: Stationary magnetic poles surround the wound armature. Brushes and commutator transfer and switch current as the armature rotates.

steps.title: Reduce speed
steps.text: The armature sun gear drives three planets inside a fixed ring. Their carrier delivers slower rotation to the output shaft.

steps.title: Engage briefly
steps.text: The solenoid and lever shift the drive toward the flywheel. A provisional slotted clevis and fork groove maintain geometric connection across the prescribed stroke. The viewer keeps the ten-tooth pinion retracted; sampled geometry checks do not implement a loaded starting sequence.

steps.title: Keep the application distinction
steps.text: The truck parts page separates manual F2TZ11002ARM from automatic F7SZ11002AARM. A matching tooth count alone does not establish mounting depth or interchangeability.

troubleshooting.title: Slow or abnormal cranking
troubleshooting.text: The factory load test compares measured starter current under engine load with the applicable electrical specification. The CAD model measures neither current nor battery condition; its geometric gear checks are not a diagnostic test.
